## assist-classical-levine-morelia-dimension-one-omission: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: https://www.esaga.uni-due.de/f/marc.levine/publ/Morelia.pdf; printed/PDF p. 24, Theorem 3.14; p. 24 immediately following paragraph identifying the modified Chow group with ordinary CH for smooth X.

Claim: Theorem 3.14 states torsion-freeness of the modified top Chow group for a reduced affine variety of dimension d over any algebraically closed field, without excluding dimension one.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Context checked: Part 1 introduction and sections 1.1–1.2 (pp. 3–4), the section-3 opening (p. 17), and sections 3.4–3.7 (pp. 21–25) impose no standing dimension-at-least-two hypothesis. Section 3.4 explicitly discusses curves. Section 3.7 restarts with an affine variety over a field, and Theorem 3.14 quantifies dimension d without a lower bound. Take $k=C$ and a smooth elliptic curve E with origin O; let $U=E\setminus\{O\}$. This is a smooth reduced affine curve. Every divisor on U extends by closure to a divisor on E. A divisor on E restricts to a principal divisor on U exactly when subtracting the divisor of the same rational function leaves a divisor supported at O; hence restriction gives $Pic(U)=Pic(E)/Z[O]$. The degree map is split by the degree-one class [O], so this quotient is $Pic^0(E)$. For a nonzero n-torsion point T of E(C), $L=O_E(T-O)$ is a nontrivial degree-zero n-torsion line bundle by the elliptic-curve identification $E(C)=Pic^0(E)$. It survives the quotient: if $L=m[O]$, degree forces $m=0$, contradicting L nontrivial. Thus its restriction is nonzero torsion in $CH^1(U)$. The modified group is ordinary CH for smooth U by the source own explanation. Thus the unrestricted $d=1$ statement is false. The accompanying implication of injectivity need not fail in this example; the defect recorded is specifically torsion-freeness. This consulted source is not used in either proposed patch.

Correction: Restrict the stated torsion-freeness assertion to dimension at least two (the relevant higher-dimensional zero-cycle theorem), or separately state the dimension-one case with its possible Picard torsion. Affected scope: $d=1$ only is demonstrated here; no claim about the singular general-dimensional proof is made. Disposition: retain this confirmed source finding, exclude Theorem 3.14 as a supplier, and use the exact classification statements instead.

## assist-classical-levine-morelia-projective-monoid-not-kzero: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: https://www.esaga.uni-due.de/f/marc.levine/publ/Morelia.pdf; printed/PDF p. 3, section 1.1, paragraph beginning Alternatively immediately after Definition 1.2.

Claim: The paragraph proposes defining K0(R) as projective-module isomorphism classes modulo stable equivalence by the same projective or free summand.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: For a field $R=k$, finite projective modules are $k^n$ with $n\ge 0$. If $k^n$ plus $k^m$ is isomorphic to $k^r$ plus $k^m$, dimension forces $n=r$. The proposed quotient is therefore the additive monoid N. Definition 1.2 in the preceding paragraph instead yields the group Z, including the negative class -[k], which is absent from that quotient. Thus the proposed alternative omits group completion or virtual pairs. No standing hypothesis in section 1.1 excludes fields. This source is unused in both patches; their completed local K-zero supplier explicitly uses the group completion.

Correction: Replace the proposed alternative with the group of formal pairs of projectives modulo the stabilized relation, or specify group completion of the indicated monoid. Affected scope: the proposed alternative group construction, already false over every field; no original-article defect is inferred. Disposition: record the unused-source error and retain the completed affine K-zero supplier.

Its local-chain argument uses free projectives at local rings and then derived sheaf-map detection, without asserting global bundle generation. The immediate suppliers cover every qcqs field-scheme under the target's Choice and size assumptions. Lower-class vanishing kills both degree-three Cartan cross terms.

The doubled-plane evidence confirms the separate original representation defect. Set $A=k[u,v]$ and glue two copies of Spec A along $W=D(u)\cup D(v)$. This scheme is smooth, normal, finite type and qcqs. Quillen–Suslin trivializes chart bundles; $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O)=A_u\cap A_v=A$ extends transition matrices and inverses, so every global bundle is trivial and $\operatorname{Pic}=0$. The supported origin Koszul class has alternating homology length 1 but ambient class $1-2+1=0$. Localization supplies a class in K1(W) with nonzero supported boundary. Both chart restriction images have boundary zero, so Mayer–Vietoris produces a nonzero perfect K0 class restricting to zero on both charts. Its rank and determinant vanish; the inspected rank/Picard fiber contracts place it in F2. It cannot be a bundle difference. This defeats the printed Lemma 5.3 premise invoked by Lemma 6.4, without refuting either conclusion. Retained finding author-9f7895525f41-bundle-representation-scope remains unchanged.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: A nonempty restriction of an integral generator is integral and closed in the open ambient scheme. Codimensions at surviving generic points are unchanged, including on every coordinate face. Face intersections commute with restriction, and the local rings and lengths at surviving generic points are unchanged. Thus restriction commutes with each face map and its alternating sum. The supplied complex applies to V, which is smooth and finite type over k.

## seminormalization-finiteness-scope: dismissed

Source: The Stacks Project, [Weak normalization](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0H3I) and [Normalization](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BXR); Lemmas 29.56.3 and 29.56.7; Lemma 33.27.1(1)–(2).

Claim: The finiteness assertion might require a stronger field or scheme hypothesis.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: A scheme locally of finite type over a field is locally noetherian, so the comparison with the relative seminormalization applies. On reduced affine opens, the intermediate algebra lies in the finite normalization algebra and is therefore a finite module over the noetherian base. The seminormal source factors through the reduction. No perfectness or separatedness assumption is needed for this argument. The cited source omits or abbreviates portions of the seminormal constructions; those prerequisites were accepted as external inputs, not reconstructed.

Correction: No correction required.

Claim: The cited comparison may require finite dimension.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: The introduction states equality for a Noetherian domain without imposing finite dimension on that comparison. Its rank of a valuation overring is its Krull dimension, matching the supplied definition. When the Krull dimension is infinite, the reverse inequality follows from the standard domination of local domains by valuation overrings, so both dimensions are infinite. The item correctly treats the result as an external input and does not claim a local proof.

## monoidal-transport-strength: dismissed

Source: Hinich, Dwyer–Kan localization revisited, arXiv:1311.4128v4, §2.1.5; Lurie, Higher Algebra, Definition 2.0.0.7 and Definition 2.1.3.7; Proof steps 1.1–4.1.

Claim: The transport might be only lax symmetric monoidal.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Straightening over the product and currying give natural transformations of the entire S-diagrams. Unstraightening those transformations preserves all S-cocartesian arrows, including active and nullary operations, so the resulting transports are strong symmetric monoidal. The functor from B supplies the higher coherences.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Kasprowski–Winges define the cofiber Grothendieck group and state its comparison with π₀ of nonconnective K-theory after idempotent completion. BGT Definition 9.6 and Remark 9.33 provide the stated construction and contextual comparison in the latter passage's Waldhausen setting. The underlying comparison proofs were not reconstructed.

Correction: No correction is needed.

## supported-extension-by-zero: dismissed

Source: Generated helper lemma; Statement and proof steps 1.1–3.1.

Claim: Extension by zero might fail to preserve the perfect complexes needed for the claimed equivalence.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: For a complex supported in the closed subset T, extension by zero restricts to the original perfect complex on V and is acyclic on the open complement of T. These opens cover X, so it is locally perfect. The counit is a quasi-isomorphism stalkwise. Since V is a quasi-compact open of the quasi-separated scheme X, it is qcqs, so the stated K-theory interface applies to both schemes. The proof does not require extension by zero to preserve arbitrary quasi-coherent complexes or require X minus T to be quasi-compact.

## mvw-abstract-blowup-convention: dismissed

Source: Mazza–Voevodsky–Weibel, Lecture notes on motivic cohomology, https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/MVWnotes/xprova.pdf; Lecture 1, printed p. 5; Lecture 12, printed pp. 91 and 96–98, especially Definitions 12.21 and 12.23, Example 12.24, Lemma 12.26, and Propositions 12.27–12.28.

Claim: The difference between the source’s abstract-blowup convention and the supplied interface invalidates the topology comparison.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: The source permits an isomorphism on reduced complements, while the interface requires an isomorphism on the complements themselves. Nevertheless, every source abstract-blowup coproduct is proper and completely decomposed, because reduction preserves points and residue fields. Conversely, every interface abstract blowup is a source abstract blowup, and source Lemma 12.26 makes every completely decomposed proper map a source cover. The two generated topologies therefore agree. The source’s Proposition 12.28 supplies the stated refinement, including factorization through the original covering morphism. I read the cited source pages and the printed proofs of Lemma 12.26 and Propositions 12.27–12.28; I did not independently reconstruct the flattening input or the full SV00 theory.

Correction: No correction is required.

Source: [Elmanto–Morrow v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.08463v1); Theorem8.2 footnote14; criterion External input.

Claim: Degreewise pro-cohomological vanishing was equated unconditionally with categorical cartesianness.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Historical fatal generated overstatement. The current criterion, relative package and shifted proof already use degreewise vanishing only. That suffices for Proposition8.10’s application. Assessment recorded in job-02061: the criterion, relative package, shifted-hypotheses and fiber-bound arguments were read. They use degreewise pro-cohomology vanishing only; the fixed shift preserves it and the fixed-degree modification argument suffices. Independently checked $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r}Z[m]$ with tail inclusions: every fixed cohomology pro-group is zero and the complexes are uniformly bounded above, but every transition $C_s\to C_r$ is nonzero on $H^{-s}$. This defeats the generic unbounded pro-derived inference, not the geometric theorem. Fresh served EM v1 HTML footnote 14 still contains that justification; its title date is 24 August 2026, so this is not authentication of immutable September 2023 bytes. **Assumptions to strengthen:** A uniform two-sided amplitude bound would permit finite Postnikov detection; no such bound is being silently assumed here.

**Redundant assumptions:** None identified.

**Conclusions to weaken:** Retain the degreewise pro-cohomology condition actually used by the criterion.

**Silent assumptions:** A uniform upper bound alone makes pro-cohomology conservative on unbounded pro-derived objects.

**Definitions to clarify:** Degreewise zero pro-cohomology is distinct from zero in unbounded Pro(D(Z)).

**Counterexample:** $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r} Z[m]$, $r\ge 0$, with tail inclusions is uniformly bounded above and degreewise pro-zero but is nonzero in Pro(D(Z)).

For fixed a, $H^a(C_r)=0$ once $r>-a$, so every pro-cohomology group is zero. For $s\ge r$, $C_s\to C_r$ induces the identity $Z\to Z$ on $H^{-s}$; no transition to stage r is zero. A zero pro-object would have an eventually zero transition to each stage. Thus uniform upper boundedness does not give the claimed categorical detection.

Counterexample limits: The generic categorical inference is refuted. No counterexample to the specific geometric pro-cdh assertion is supplied.

The cited theorem statements and valuative definitions were inspected; the filtration construction and Jaffard results underlying EHIK were not reconstructed.

Source: Elmanto–Morrow, Motivic cohomology of equicharacteristic schemes, arXiv:2309.08463v1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.08463v1; Proofs of Theorem 4.12(1), p. 23, and Theorem 4.27(1), p. 29.

Claim: The printed proofs assert respectively that the motivic stage $\operatorname{Fil}^j K(X)$ is supported in homological degrees at least d+1−j and d+2−j.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: For X the spectrum of the relevant prime field, $d=0$ and $\operatorname{Fil}^0 K(X)=K(X)$, whose π₀ is ℤ. At $j=0$, either printed estimate would force π₀ to vanish. These are errors in the displayed proof estimates; this counterexample does not refute the separately stated boundedness theorem. The assigned lemma explicitly avoids relying on those estimates. Report classification: the recorded local wording, scope or display correction is easily-fixable; this does not promote it to a false theorem.

Correction: Do not import the printed numerical estimates. The source's stated boundedness, interpreted using §2.2, supplies an unspecified B(X) with stage r supported in homotopical degrees at least r−B(X). No corrected numerical value is established here.

## spectral-kzero-stability-missing-bundle-hypothesis: confirmed — 1. Missing prerequisites

Source: Generated prerequisite item; current affine comparison and stabilization suppliers; Statement; Facts F1–F3; proof steps 1.1 and 2.1.

Claim: Equality of spectral K-zero classes is equivalent to the displayed free stabilization, without specifying that E and F are vector bundles.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Confirmed fatal generated omission, with a repair proposed. Over $A=k[t]$, the perfect module A/(t) has class zero by the resolution $0\to A\to A\to A/(t)\to0$, but $A/(t)\oplus A^N$ cannot be isomorphic to $A^N$ because its nonzero torsion persists. All supplied equivalences require vector bundles. The direct cancellation consumer already uses bundles; its universe assumptions are made explicit. The five later consumers retain their interfaces and arguments. This finding concerns the generated helper, not an original article defect. Both retained prior responses were consulted only for this concern; their unapplied proposals confer no acceptance. Assessment recorded in job-02061: the current stability helper explicitly quantifies vector bundles E,F, a commutative unital noetherian ring, AC and compatible universes. Its proof passes through the affine perfect/bundle comparison and common free stabilization, as required by the cancellation application. No stabilization theorem for arbitrary derived objects is asserted.

Correction: Specify finite locally free E,F and the existing comparison universes, retain AC and noetherian affineness, and verify both directions using the unchanged suppliers. Carry the universe assumptions into the direct consumer. Original article coverage and all other inspected content remain unchanged.

**Redundant assumptions:** None identified.

**Conclusions to weaken:** None identified.

**Silent assumptions:** None identified.

**Definitions to clarify:** None identified.

**Counterexample:** $A=k[t]$, $M=A/(t)$ has perfect spectral $K_0$ class zero but cannot stabilize to zero by the same finite free summand.

Its resolution $0\to A\xrightarrow{t} A\to M\to 0$ gives $[M]=[A]-[A]=0$. $M\oplus A^N$ retains nonzero t-torsion, while $A^N$ is torsion-free.

Counterexample limits: Refutes the former unrestricted module/perfect-object formulation, not the current vector-bundle statement.

Source: Assigned item, steps 1.1–2.1; [Stacks Project, Lemma 28.7.5](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0357), [Section 28.12](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/033P), [Lemma 33.25.8](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04QM), and [Lemma 33.20.3](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06LF); Statement and Proof; article p. 15, Theorem 6.7.

Claim: The construction remains valid when a normal scheme of dimension at most three has components of different dimensions.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Normality and Noetherianity give finitely many clopen integral components. On each three-dimensional component, the perfect-field smooth locus is the regular locus; (R1) excludes codimension-zero and codimension-one points from its complement. The finite-type dimension formula bounds that complement by one. Adding the lower-dimensional clopen components gives a closed complement of dimension at most two. The pure-dimensional case has no such additional components. The empty smooth stratum is explicitly permitted. The cited Stacks statements and printed proofs relevant to these uses were inspected; their deeper referenced commutative-algebra proofs were not reconstructed.

Correction: None required.

Source: [Swan 1974, primary GDZ scans](https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/id/PPN356556735_0027), Inventiones Mathematicae27,23–43, DOI10.1007/BF01389963; Theorem1.4 free-chart reduction, printed pp.26–27; assigned Proof1.1–3.1.

Claim: The printed proof treats geometric integrality as local on an arbitrary open cover.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Confirmed nonfatal source inference gap. The zero scheme of (x(x−1),y) in A³ is two disjoint lines, while its intersections with the covering opens D(x) and D(x−1) are geometrically integral lines. This refutes the inference, not the theorem. The current proof instead ensures a common nonempty open dense in every chart curve, also after field extension. Visually read the hash-verified p.23 variety convention, Theorems1.3–1.4 and their complete printed proof on pp.26–28. Checked the free-chart controlling family, infinite-field hypothesis, rank two and unimodular pair (0,1). Did not reconstruct the cited classical Bertini foundations or read the entire paper. Assessment recorded in job-02061: primary p.27 does invoke locality for the conditions including integrality. The local-to-global inference alone is false: V(x(x-1))⊂A² has integral nonempty restrictions to D(x) and D(x-1) but is disconnected. The current common-core and chartwise-integrality helpers were read: all chart curves share a nonempty dense open, and the argument persists after field extension. They avoid the false premise. Retain this consulted-source proof gap separately from the terminal sign typo and from the validity of the theorem's conclusion.

Correction: Retain the source finding and the current common-core argument. The application uses the free-chart external input, not the faulty arbitrary-cover inference; no change to the gluing proof is needed.

Source: [Swan 1974 primary scan 30](https://gdz.sub.uni-goettingen.de/iiif/image/gdz:PPN356556735_0027:00000030/full/1400,/0/default.jpg); Theorem 1.1(1), printed p.24.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Retained prior-response ID, duplicating provisional-swan-1974-bertini-dimension-symbol. Assessment recorded in job-02061: visually read primary p.24. The subspace has dimension r in $A^n$, but the intersection dimension is printed $d-r$. For $V=A^3$ and $r=1$ the actual intersection is a line, not a surface. The correct expected dimension is $d+r-n$. Correction: Use d+r−n without counting a second defect.

Source: Generated prerequisite; article weight-one comparison p.4; Statement, second sentence; Proof2.1.

Claim: The degree-(n+1) isomorphism needs vanishing in degree n+2.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Confirmed fatal duplicate. The mapping-cone exact sequence and counterexample establish the correction directly. The downstream exact-range and weight-one arguments remain valid. Assessment recorded in job-02061: read the actual current cone helper and weight-one consumer. The corrected proof uses $H^{i-1}(C)$ and $H^i(C)$. For $f:0\to Z[-n-2]$, $H^{n+1}(f)$ is $0\to 0$ although $H^{n+2}(C)=Z$, disproving only the historical necessity clause. Current sufficient bounds and the consumer's degree range are sound. These duplicate IDs remain confirmed historical generated defects, with no new repair.

Correction: Apply the shared cone repair while retaining all three finding IDs.

## adjudicate-a8be8a17c858-unbounded-pro-cdh-equivalence: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: [Elmanto–Morrow v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.08463v1); generated interfaces; Theorem8.2 footnote14; criterion and shifted proof1.1.

Claim: Degreewise zero pro-cohomology and a uniform upper bound imply zero in unbounded Pro(D(Z)).

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Confirmed false inference: $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r}Z[m]$ is uniformly bounded above and degreewise pro-zero, but has no zero transition. Current generated bodies already avoid it. This does not refute the particular geometric categorical assertion. Assessment recorded in job-02061: the criterion, relative package, shifted-hypotheses and fiber-bound arguments were read. They use degreewise pro-cohomology vanishing only; the fixed shift preserves it and the fixed-degree modification argument suffices. Independently checked $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r}Z[m]$ with tail inclusions: every fixed cohomology pro-group is zero and the complexes are uniformly bounded above, but every transition $C_s\to C_r$ is nonzero on $H^{-s}$. This defeats the generic unbounded pro-derived inference, not the geometric theorem. Fresh served EM v1 HTML footnote 14 still contains that justification; its title date is 24 August 2026, so this is not authentication of immutable September 2023 bytes. Retain the source and generated errors separately.

Correction: Preserve the current degreewise convention and this version-qualified source finding.

**Assumptions to strengthen:** A uniform two-sided amplitude bound would permit finite Postnikov detection; no such bound is being silently assumed here.

**Redundant assumptions:** None identified.

**Conclusions to weaken:** Retain the degreewise pro-cohomology condition actually used by the criterion.

**Silent assumptions:** A uniform upper bound alone makes pro-cohomology conservative on unbounded pro-derived objects.

**Definitions to clarify:** Degreewise zero pro-cohomology is distinct from zero in unbounded Pro(D(Z)).

**Counterexample:** $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r} Z[m]$, $r\ge 0$, with tail inclusions is uniformly bounded above and degreewise pro-zero but is nonzero in Pro(D(Z)).

For fixed a, $H^a(C_r)=0$ once $r>-a$, so every pro-cohomology group is zero. For $s\ge r$, $C_s\to C_r$ induces the identity $Z\to Z$ on $H^{-s}$; no transition to stage r is zero. A zero pro-object would have an eventually zero transition to each stage. Thus uniform upper boundedness does not give the claimed categorical detection.

Counterexample limits: The generic categorical inference is refuted. No counterexample to the specific geometric pro-cdh assertion is supplied.

## adjudicate-a8be8a17c858-em-v1-unbounded-pro-equivalence: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: [Elmanto–Morrow, arXiv:2309.08463v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.08463v1); Theorem 8.2, footnote 14, p.54; Proposition 8.10 modification step, p.57.

Claim: Degreewise zero pro-cohomology detects zero unbounded pro-derived objects under only a uniform upper bound.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Confirmed source inference error; nonfatal to this application. Independently, $C_r=\bigoplus_{n\ge r}\mathbb Z[n]$ with tail inclusions has eventually zero cohomology in each fixed degree, while every transition $C_s\to C_r$ remains nonzero on $H^{-s}$. The current imports explicitly exclude this inference. Their degreewise condition survives the fixed shift and suffices for the criterion’s fixed-degree modification argument. The inspected version is v1 only. Assessment recorded in job-02061: the criterion, relative package, shifted-hypotheses and fiber-bound arguments were read. They use degreewise pro-cohomology vanishing only; the fixed shift preserves it and the fixed-degree modification argument suffices. Independently checked $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r}Z[m]$ with tail inclusions: every fixed cohomology pro-group is zero and the complexes are uniformly bounded above, but every transition $C_s\to C_r$ is nonzero on $H^{-s}$. This defeats the generic unbounded pro-derived inference, not the geometric theorem. Fresh served EM v1 HTML footnote 14 still contains that justification; its title date is 24 August 2026, so this is not authentication of immutable September 2023 bytes. Retain the source and generated errors separately. This pass: Checked the degreewise convention in the current criterion, relative package, shifted-hypotheses and fiber-bound records, and read the actual EM footnote. The tail complexes $\bigoplus_{m\ge r} Z[m]$ are uniformly bounded above and have degreewise pro-zero cohomology, but every tail transition is nonzero on $H^{-s}$. This refutes the generic unbounded pro-derived detection inference. Current applications do not make that inference; the geometric theorem itself is not refuted.

Correction: Preserve the source finding separately from the repaired generated contracts. Retain the current degreewise convention; no further assigned-item change is necessary.

Affected items: thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-dimension-criterion-input, thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-relative-package-input, lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-shifted-hypotheses, lem-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-prime-field-vanishing

**Assumptions to strengthen:** A uniform two-sided amplitude bound would permit finite Postnikov detection; no such bound is being silently assumed here.

**Redundant assumptions:** None identified.

**Conclusions to weaken:** Retain the degreewise pro-cohomology condition actually used by the criterion.

**Silent assumptions:** A uniform upper bound alone makes pro-cohomology conservative on unbounded pro-derived objects.

**Definitions to clarify:** Degreewise zero pro-cohomology is distinct from zero in unbounded Pro(D(Z)).

**Counterexample:** $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r} Z[m]$, $r\ge 0$, with tail inclusions is uniformly bounded above and degreewise pro-zero but is nonzero in Pro(D(Z)).

For fixed a, $H^a(C_r)=0$ once $r>-a$, so every pro-cohomology group is zero. For $s\ge r$, $C_s\to C_r$ induces the identity $Z\to Z$ on $H^{-s}$; no transition to stage r is zero. A zero pro-object would have an eventually zero transition to each stage. Thus uniform upper boundedness does not give the claimed categorical detection.

Counterexample limits: The generic categorical inference is refuted. No counterexample to the specific geometric pro-cdh assertion is supplied.

## source-weibel-ii-7-7-1-minimum-pd-bound: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: Charles Weibel, [The K-book, Chapter II](https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~weibel/Kbook/Kbook.II.pdf), cached PDF SHA256 529ea8a5853e9fa55279e7ad79047155409b10847bd924b56f708f0950ebc607; Definition 7.7, pp. 66–67; Lemma 7.7.1 and Corollary 7.7.2, p. 67.

Claim: Lemma 7.7.1 prints the kernel resolution-length bound min{m,n−1}.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: The bound is false: for the split sequence 0 → k[t]/(t) → (k[t]/(t))² → k[t]/(t) → 0, both middle and quotient modules have projective dimension one, but the printed bound would make the kernel projective. The assigned item does not use that bound; the displayed finite truncated-cone construction supplies the kernel closure needed for the resolution comparison. Assessment recorded in job-02061: visually read the supplied author-PDF p.67 image. The bound is printed as min{m,n-1}. Over k[t], the split exact sequence with kernel and quotient k[t]/(t) and middle term their direct sum has all three projective dimensions one. The printed minimum would make the kernel projective, which is false. Use a maximum with the appropriate zero boundary convention. The current resolution comparison supplies its own finite-cone argument and does not use the false estimate. No final printed-book or errata verification is claimed.

Correction: Replace the minimum by max{m,n−1}, with the appropriate nonnegative boundary convention. Retain the source qualification and do not use the false bound.

They use degreewise pro-cohomology vanishing only; the fixed shift preserves it and the fixed-degree modification argument suffices. Independently checked $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r}Z[m]$ with tail inclusions: every fixed cohomology pro-group is zero and the complexes are uniformly bounded above, but every transition $C_s\to C_r$ is nonzero on $H^{-s}$. **Definitions to clarify:** Degreewise zero pro-cohomology is distinct from zero in unbounded Pro(D(Z)).

**Counterexample:** $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r} Z[m]$, $r\ge 0$, with tail inclusions is uniformly bounded above and degreewise pro-zero but is nonzero in Pro(D(Z)).

For fixed a, $H^a(C_r)=0$ once $r>-a$, so every pro-cohomology group is zero. For $s\ge r$, $C_s\to C_r$ induces the identity $Z\to Z$ on $H^{-s}$; no transition to stage r is zero. A zero pro-object would have an eventually zero transition to each stage. Thus uniform upper boundedness does not give the claimed categorical detection.

Counterexample limits: The generic categorical inference is refuted. No counterexample to the specific geometric pro-cdh assertion is supplied.

**Definitions to clarify:** Degreewise zero pro-cohomology is distinct from zero in unbounded Pro(D(Z)).

**Counterexample:** $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r} Z[m]$, $r\ge 0$, with tail inclusions is uniformly bounded above and degreewise pro-zero but is nonzero in Pro(D(Z)).

For fixed a, $H^a(C_r)=0$ once $r>-a$, so every pro-cohomology group is zero. For $s\ge r$, $C_s\to C_r$ induces the identity $Z\to Z$ on $H^{-s}$; no transition to stage r is zero. A zero pro-object would have an eventually zero transition to each stage. Thus uniform upper boundedness does not give the claimed categorical detection.

## adjudicate-e3a1a72ced00-em-v1-unbounded-pro-inference: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: [Elmanto–Morrow v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.08463v1); Theorem 8.2, footnote 14, p. 54; Proposition 8.10 modification step; current imports’ External input sections.

Claim: Uniform boundedness above alone identifies degreewise pro-acyclicity with zero in Pro(D(Z)).

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Confirmed nonfatal defect in the general source justification. Independently checked the tail system $C_n=\bigoplus_{r\ge n}Z[r]$: it is uniformly bounded above and degreewise pro-zero, but no transition to a fixed stage is zero. This does not refute actual motivic descent. Both current imports exclude the inference. The inspected modification argument requires only fixed-degree pro exactness. Assessment recorded in job-02061: the criterion, relative package, shifted-hypotheses and fiber-bound arguments were read. They use degreewise pro-cohomology vanishing only; the fixed shift preserves it and the fixed-degree modification argument suffices. Independently checked $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r}Z[m]$ with tail inclusions: every fixed cohomology pro-group is zero and the complexes are uniformly bounded above, but every transition $C_s\to C_r$ is nonzero on $H^{-s}$. This defeats the generic unbounded pro-derived inference, not the geometric theorem. Fresh served EM v1 HTML footnote 14 still contains that justification; its title date is 24 August 2026, so this is not authentication of immutable September 2023 bytes. Retain the source and generated errors separately.

Correction: Preserve degreewise pro-cdh descent and the source-version qualification. No further repair or stronger pro-derived assertion is proposed.

Affected items: thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-dimension-criterion-input, thm-author-0bac6b264f4a-motivic-dim-relative-package-input, thm-motivic-dimension-vanishing

**Assumptions to strengthen:** A uniform two-sided amplitude bound would permit finite Postnikov detection; no such bound is being silently assumed here.

**Redundant assumptions:** None identified.

**Conclusions to weaken:** Retain the degreewise pro-cohomology condition actually used by the criterion.

**Silent assumptions:** A uniform upper bound alone makes pro-cohomology conservative on unbounded pro-derived objects.

**Definitions to clarify:** Degreewise zero pro-cohomology is distinct from zero in unbounded Pro(D(Z)).

**Counterexample:** $C_r=\bigoplus_{m\ge r} Z[m]$, $r\ge 0$, with tail inclusions is uniformly bounded above and degreewise pro-zero but is nonzero in Pro(D(Z)).

For fixed a, $H^a(C_r)=0$ once $r>-a$, so every pro-cohomology group is zero. For $s\ge r$, $C_s\to C_r$ induces the identity $Z\to Z$ on $H^{-s}$; no transition to stage r is zero. A zero pro-object would have an eventually zero transition to each stage. Thus uniform upper boundedness does not give the claimed categorical detection.

Counterexample limits: The generic categorical inference is refuted. No counterexample to the specific geometric pro-cdh assertion is supplied.

## consumer-978448e68c43-generic-open-boundary: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: Current generated proof and actual coherent-dévis­sage supplier hypotheses; Facts F2; proof steps 1.1–4.1.

Claim: The proof incorrectly treats every closed point of a nonempty open as distinct from the generic point.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Confirmed nonfatal generated boundary error. For the spectrum of a DVR, the generic-point singleton is open. On that open, its residue-field class has rank one, and removing it leaves the empty set, contradicting the intermediate proof assertions. The lemma’s conclusions remain valid. The affine-only residue-sheaf supplier also needs an explicit local-coherence argument for the general scheme application.

Correction: Generate each open’s G0 using its structure sheaf and residue sheaves only at points distinct from the generic point. Remove only those points in the colimit argument. Verify global residue-sheaf coherence on an affine neighbourhood and its complementary open. Preserve the full Noetherian scope.

## finding-em-810-modification-proof-notation: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: Elmanto and Morrow, Motivic cohomology of equicharacteristic schemes, arXiv:2309.08463v1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.08463v1; Proposition 8.10 proof, p. 57, modification construction.

Claim: The printed modification argument refers to the closure of U in X′ and to X′ ×_X X2 as a Nisnevich cover of X′.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: At that point X′ is being constructed, while X2 → X1 is the Nisnevich cover; its composite with X1 → X need not be Nisnevich. This is a defect in the displayed source argument, not a counterexample to the imported criterion. Assessment recorded in job-02061: the complete short Proposition 8.10 proof was read in served EM v1 HTML. The indicated closure-in-X-prime and fiber product over X remain printed there. The needed construction is the reduced closure of a dense-open section inside $X_1$, followed by $X^{\prime}\times_{X_1}X_2$. The current import uses the criterion with the degreewise modification application, not that malformed notation as a new local proof. This is a nonfatal version-qualified source proof-line error, not a refutation of the criterion.

Correction: Choose a section of the proper cdp cover X1 → X over a dense open U, take the reduced closure of its image in X1 as X′, and pull the Nisnevich cover back as X′ ×_{X1} X2 → X′.

## author-6542695536e1-support-indexing-notation: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: Fasel–Yakerson, Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds, arXiv:2610.22679v1; Definitions 2.2 and 2.7, PDF pp. 4 and 6.

Claim: The original support-indexing display needs a shift or an explicit shifted-realization convention.

Localization sends a class in $K_1$ of the overlap onto the length-one origin class, whose ambient Euler class is $1-2+1=0$; Mayer-Vietoris injects the resulting Z cokernel into perfect $K_0$ of the doubled plane. ## article-qcqs-smooth-locus-proof-scope: confirmed — 2. Genuine but easily fixable defect

Source: [Article v1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22679v1); Conventions p.3; Lemmas 5.1–5.2 proofs p.10.

Claim: Normality ensures dense smooth locus and injective Picard restriction throughout the qcqs category.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: Confirmed nonfatal original proof-scope defect, distinct from the generated narrowing. Article v1 p. 3 conventions and the complete p. 10 proof were read in text and images. For X=$\mathbb P^1$ over k(t), viewed over algebraically closed k, the k-smooth locus is empty although X is normal qcqs and Pic(X)=Z. Indeed a nonempty smooth affine open would have a nonzero finitely generated k-algebra containing k(t); a maximal residue field k would give an impossible k-algebra map k(t) to k. Thus the broad smooth-locus premise fails, while the Chern-projection equality is supplied by the alternate perfect-class argument. The finite-type smooth-restriction consequence is retained. Assessment recorded in job-02061: the article really uses unrestricted normality in its standing qcqs category, rather than a global finite-type hypothesis. Spec k(t) is normal qcqs but has empty k-smooth locus, since k(t) is not a finitely presented k-algebra. $\mathbb P^1_{k(t)}$ likewise has no k-smooth points while Pic is Z. Thus the source's unrestricted smooth-locus restriction premise fails. The current determinant/unit and rank/Picard arguments retain the normal qcqs conclusions by alternate proofs. The finite-type smooth-locus lemma remains valid with its actual hypotheses; this is a proof-scope defect, not a counterexample to the Chern identities. This pass: The nonaffine example $\mathbb P^1$ over k(t), viewed as a k-scheme, is the unambiguous counterexample within the article's standing normal-qcqs scope: it has empty k-smooth locus, global functions k(t), and Picard group Z. Spec k(t) demonstrates the general qcqs phenomenon but does not satisfy the separate printed convention that affine schemes are finite type over k. Neither example refutes the lemma's conclusion. The current actual determinant and first-layer arguments do not use the false premise.

Correction: Retain this original article defect after repair. Use the actual rank-zero-stage and perfect-first-class constructions for the qcqs equality and retain smooth restriction and Picard injection only under the additional finite-type hypotheses.

The field k(t) is not a finitely generated k-algebra by Zariski's lemma. Its only nonempty open is itself, so no point has a smooth finite-presentation neighbourhood. Global functions and units on the empty smooth locus cannot recover k(t) and k(t)^×.

**Counterexample:** For $X=P^1_{k(t)}$ viewed over algebraically closed k, restriction Pic(X) to the k-smooth locus is not injective.

Every hypothetical smooth affine neighbourhood would be a nonzero finite-type k-algebra containing k(t). A maximal residue field would be k, impossible for a k-algebra embedding of k(t) into k. Hence the k-smooth locus is empty, whereas $\operatorname{Pic}(P^1_{k(t)})=\mathbb{Z}$.

Counterexample limits: These disprove the smooth-locus premises, not the current low-layer conclusions. For original-article scope use the nonaffine $P^1_{k(t)}$ example; the affine Spec k(t) example is only an ambient-qcqs illustration.

## low-filtration-original-smooth-locus-gap: confirmed — 3. Genuine substantial defect

Source: Fasel–Yakerson, Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds, arXiv:2610.22679v1; PDF pp. 3 and 8–9, notation and conventions and proof of Lemma 4.1.

Claim: The original proof uses normality to identify global functions on X with those on its smooth locus.

Retained native history; its earlier reading and repair claims are not fresh reading in this assessment: That assertion does not follow throughout the stated normal qcqs scope. For example, X = Spec k(t) is normal and qcqs over the algebraically closed field k, but its structure morphism is not locally of finite presentation, so its smooth locus over k is empty. The article’s restriction argument therefore does not establish this case. This is a defect in the original proof, not a counterexample to the lemma. The current proof instead uses the determinant-projection supplier with the matching qcqs hypotheses. Assessment recorded in job-02061: the article really uses unrestricted normality in its standing qcqs category, rather than a global finite-type hypothesis. Spec k(t) is normal qcqs but has empty k-smooth locus, since k(t) is not a finitely presented k-algebra. $\mathbb P^1_{k(t)}$ likewise has no k-smooth points while Pic is Z. Thus the source's unrestricted smooth-locus restriction premise fails. The current determinant/unit and rank/Picard arguments retain the normal qcqs conclusions by alternate proofs. The finite-type smooth-locus lemma remains valid with its actual hypotheses; this is a proof-scope defect, not a counterexample to the Chern identities. This pass: The nonaffine example $\mathbb P^1$ over k(t), viewed as a k-scheme, is the unambiguous counterexample within the article's standing normal-qcqs scope: it has empty k-smooth locus, global functions k(t), and Picard group Z. Spec k(t) demonstrates the general qcqs phenomenon but does not satisfy the separate printed convention that affine schemes are finite type over k. Neither example refutes the lemma's conclusion. The current actual determinant and first-layer arguments do not use the false premise.

Correction: Retain the normal qcqs statement and use the supplied surjectivity of the actual weight-one projection, as in the current argument.

Affected items: lem-low-filtration-homotopy

**Assumptions to strengthen:** Finite type over the algebraically closed field suffices for the printed smooth-locus/Hartogs route; the corrected actual-map argument needs no such narrowing.

**Redundant assumptions:** None identified.

**Conclusions to weaken:** None identified.

**Silent assumptions:** Normal qcqs schemes have a dense smooth locus over the specified field.

**Definitions to clarify:** Smooth means smooth over the stated base field, including local finite presentation.

**Counterexample:** X=Spec k(t) has empty k-smooth locus although it is normal and qcqs.

The field k(t) is not a finitely generated k-algebra by Zariski's lemma. Its only nonempty open is itself, so no point has a smooth finite-presentation neighbourhood. Global functions and units on the empty smooth locus cannot recover k(t) and k(t)^×.

**Counterexample:** For $X=P^1_{k(t)}$ viewed over algebraically closed k, restriction Pic(X) to the k-smooth locus is not injective.

Every hypothetical smooth affine neighbourhood would be a nonzero finite-type k-algebra containing k(t). A maximal residue field would be k, impossible for a k-algebra embedding of k(t) into k. Hence the k-smooth locus is empty, whereas $\operatorname{Pic}(P^1_{k(t)})=\mathbb{Z}$.

Counterexample limits: These disprove the smooth-locus premises, not the current low-layer conclusions. For original-article scope use the nonaffine $P^1_{k(t)}$ example; the affine Spec k(t) example is only an ambient-qcqs illustration.

## Limitations

- This is a research-portal assessment, not library publication, an audit stamp, proof acceptance, or exhaustive mathematical certainty. No content was altered, no serving files were written, no workers were launched, and no repair was authored or independently self-judged in this pass.
- All 96 original inventory entries and current replacements, all 18 extracted PDF pages, and all 612 native finding claims, dispositions and corrections were reviewed. The complete rich histories are retained from the hash-authenticated genuine job-02061 response, rather than the older embedded assessment. The original Euler item still maps to its current status remark. All 96 coverage rows remain unchanged.
- Earlier reading and repair claims inside retained findings are historical. Their former Current assessment labels are now explicitly attributed to job-02061. Only this report's This pass notes and appended primary-source entries describe new reading. Historical confirmations/dismissals were not promoted into independent re-audits of every supplier or source.
- Fifteen focused prerequisite bodies were opened for the requested cone, localized-base, relative-comparison, negative-image, stability, pro-cdh, Bertini, top-torsion, Murthy and fixed-ambient checks.
